bank.module: Session 1 — Relational Databases & Data Modeling for Data Engineers
bank.title: Session 1 — Data Modeling Process, Normalization, Warehousing Schemas & Constraints — Bank 002

questions.question: A project team has finished identifying business requirements and high-level entities, and is about to translate them into a structured logical design before choosing storage details. Which transition best matches the course modeling process?

options.text: Physical Data Model → Conceptual Data Model
Conceptual Data Model → Logical Data Model
Database Instance → ER notation
Snowflake Schema → Hierarchical Model

explanation.ar: الـ process في المادة يبدأ Conceptual ثم Logical ثم Physical؛ بعد high-level business view الخطوة التالية هي Logical design.

questions.question: A team is still discussing business requirements and high-level entities before deciding data types or indexes. Which modeling level is closest to this stage?

options.text: Database instance
Conceptual data model
Document model
Physical data model

explanation.ar: الـ Conceptual Data Model هو المستوى الأعلى المرتبط بفهم business requirements والعلاقات العامة قبل التفاصيل المنطقية والفيزيائية.

questions.question: Two backups taken on Monday and Friday contain different row values, but both follow the same tables, fields, data types, and relationships. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: They are different schemas because row values changed
Neither contains data because schemas never allow values
They are the same instance because schema is unchanged
They are different database instances governed by the same schema

explanation.ar: الـ schema هو التصميم الثابت نسبيًا، أما actual values في لحظة معينة فهي database instance؛ لذلك ممكن instances تختلف مع نفس schema.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the schema rather than to a changing database instance?

options.text: Table names, fields, data types, and relationships
Today's current row values only
The values inserted by users this morning
A one-time query result snapshot

explanation.ar: المادة بتوضح إن schema بيشمل structural constraints زي table names وfields وdata types والعلاقات، مش القيم الحالية نفسها.

questions.question: A database keeps the same table design for months while rows are inserted and updated every day. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The database instance never changes once created
The schema may remain stable while database instances change over time
Schema and instance are identical concepts
The schema must change every time one row changes

explanation.ar: الـ instance هو snapshot للقيم الحالية ولذلك بيتغير، بينما الـ schema غالبًا يفضل ثابت لأنه بيوصف التصميم.

questions.question: A table repeats the same student details across many subject rows, causing redundancy and update inconsistencies. Which design process from the session directly targets this problem?

options.text: Adding more repeating columns
Normalization
Removing all keys
Changing the model to a document store regardless of requirements

explanation.ar: Normalization في المادة هدفها تنظيم tables/attributes لتقليل redundancy وdependency، وده بالضبط يعالج تكرار نفس البيانات ومشاكل التحديث.

questions.question: In a relation, every StudentID always determines exactly one StudentName. Which statement best describes StudentID → StudentName using the course terminology?

options.text: It is an M:N cardinality ratio
It is a functional dependency
It is total participation
It is a multivalued attribute

explanation.ar: Functional Dependency معناها قيمة attribute أو مجموعة attributes تحدد قيمة attribute آخر؛ هنا StudentID يحدد StudentName.

questions.question: An attribute's value can be determined only when the entire composite primary key is known. Which dependency type is this?

options.text: Multivalued participation
Full functional dependency
Partial functional dependency
Transitive functional dependency

explanation.ar: Full Functional Dependency معناها إن الـ non-key attribute يعتمد على الـ whole Primary Key، مش جزء منه.

questions.question: A table has composite key (StudentID, Subject), but Teacher is determined by Subject alone. What type of dependency is present?

options.text: Partial functional dependency
Total participation
Full functional dependency
No functional dependency

explanation.ar: لأن Teacher بيتحدد بجزء واحد من الـ composite key وهو Subject، فدي Partial Functional Dependency.

source.reference: Slides 52 and 56 — Partial Functional Dependency / 2NF example

questions.question: StudentID determines ZipCode, and ZipCode determines City. What dependency pattern does this illustrate for City?

options.text: Transitive functional dependency
Partial functional dependency
No dependency
Multivalued attribute mapping

explanation.ar: City معتمد على ZipCode، وZipCode نفسه معتمد على الـ key؛ ده Transitive Dependency لأن non-key attribute بيحدد non-key attribute آخر.

source.reference: Slides 52 and 58 — Transitive Functional Dependency / 3NF example

questions.question: A designer tries to normalize a table but leaves several Subject values in one cell for each student. Which first-stage requirement has not been satisfied?

options.text: 2NF, because every key must be composite
1NF, because repeating or multivalued groups have not been removed
3NF, because every table must be a snowflake
Physical modeling, because indexes are missing

explanation.ar: قبل 2NF و3NF لازم 1NF تتحقق. وجود multiple subject values داخل cell واحد يعني إن القيم لسه مش atomic/repeating groups لسه موجودة.

questions.question: A relation is in 1NF and uses composite key (OrderID, ProductID). ProductName depends only on ProductID. Which normal form rule identifies the next issue?

options.text: 1NF, because ProductName is a repeating group
Star Schema, because every composite key is a fact table
3NF, because ProductName determines the primary key
2NF, because a non-key attribute depends on only part of the composite key

explanation.ar: دي Partial Functional Dependency على جزء من الـ composite key، و2NF هي المرحلة اللي تزيل النوع ده من الاعتماد.

questions.question: A relation has reached 2NF, but ZipCode determines City while both are non-key attributes. Which next normalization goal applies?

options.text: Convert the table to a hierarchical model
Return to 1NF and add repeating groups
Create an M:N relationship automatically
Move toward 3NF by removing the transitive dependency

explanation.ar: بعد 2NF، لو non-key attribute زي ZipCode بيحدد non-key attribute زي City، عندنا transitive dependency والهدف التالي 3NF.

questions.question: A table contains one row per student with several Subject/Grade/Teacher groups embedded inside that row. What should be addressed first?

options.text: Remove every primary key
Immediately convert it to a snowflake schema
Remove the repeating or multivalued groups to reach 1NF
Add more repeating subject columns

explanation.ar: المثال قبل 1NF فيه repeating groups/multivalued data للمواد والدرجات والمدرسين، فأول خطوة هي جعل القيم atomic وفصل التكرار.

questions.question: After the 1NF step in the course example, why is Stud_Subject separated from Student?

options.text: To make every subject a weak entity
To remove the Student primary key
To represent repeating subject-related values as separate rows instead of a multivalued group
To force a 1:1 relationship between Student and Subject

explanation.ar: فصل Stud_Subject بيحول الـ repeating group إلى rows منفصلة مرتبطة بالـ Student، وده يخلي البيانات atomic ومتوافقة مع 1NF.

questions.question: A relation is already in 1NF. What additional condition is required for 2NF?

options.text: Every table must have exactly two columns
All non-key attributes must depend on another non-key attribute
Every relationship must be M:N
Every non-key attribute must be fully functionally dependent on the primary key

explanation.ar: 2NF بتحتاج 1NF أولًا، وبعدها كل non-key attributes تعتمد على الـ whole primary key بدون partial dependency.

questions.question: In Stud_Subject(SID, Subject, Grade, Teacher), suppose the key is (SID, Subject) and Subject determines Teacher. Which decomposition matches the course's 2NF result?

options.text: Stud_Subject(SID, Teacher) only
Stud_Subject(SID, Subject, Grade) and Subject(Subject, Teacher)
Student(SID, Subject, Teacher, Grade) only
Subject(SID, Grade) and Teacher(Teacher)

explanation.ar: Teacher بيعتمد على Subject فقط، وهو جزء من composite key، فبنزيل الـ partial dependency بفصل Subject(Subject, Teacher) عن Stud_Subject.

questions.question: A designer says a table with a single-column primary key cannot suffer from partial dependency on part of that key. How does this align with the course example?

options.text: It contradicts the course because every key is composite
It means the table must be in 3NF automatically
It means functional dependency does not exist
It aligns with the note that the Student table is already 2NF because there is no composite primary key

explanation.ar: Partial Dependency بتظهر لما non-key attribute يعتمد على جزء من Composite Key. لذلك المثال بيعتبر Student table 2NF من ناحية الـ partial dependency لأنه مفيش composite PK.

questions.question: What additional rule is required to move from 2NF to 3NF in the course?

options.text: Convert all relationships to unary
Make every attribute multivalued
Remove transitive dependencies
Add repeating groups

explanation.ar: 3NF = 2NF PLUS no transitive dependencies.

questions.question: In Student(SID, SName, Birthdate, City, ZipCode), the course indicates ZipCode → City. Why is this a 3NF issue?

options.text: ZipCode and City form an M:N relationship
City is a multivalued key
City depends on a non-key attribute ZipCode, creating a transitive dependency
SID is not allowed to determine any attribute

explanation.ar: المشكلة إن SID يحدد ZipCode وZipCode يحدد City، فـ City مش dependent مباشرة على الـ key فقط؛ عندنا Transitive Dependency.

questions.question: Which decomposition best reflects the course's 3NF treatment of City and ZipCode?

options.text: Duplicate City in every subject row
Move SID into every city value as a multivalued field
Keep student data separate and create a city/zip relation so the transitive dependency is removed
Merge Student and Subject back into one repeating table

explanation.ar: المادة بتفصل بيانات City/ZipCode في relation مستقلة لتمنع non-key attribute من تحديد non-key attribute داخل Student.

questions.question: A table has no repeating groups and no partial dependency, but DepartmentName determines DepartmentLocation while both are non-key attributes. What should be investigated next?

options.text: A unary relationship by definition
A violation of 1NF caused by repeating groups
A need to add multivalued columns
A transitive dependency that may violate 3NF

explanation.ar: لو 1NF و2NF متحققين ولسه non-key attribute بيحدد non-key attribute تاني، فده Transitive Dependency وهي نقطة 3NF.

questions.question: A team attempts to reach 2NF before removing repeating groups from the original table. What is the best diagnosis?

options.text: The sequence is wrong because 2NF assumes the relation is already in 1NF
3NF must always be performed before 1NF
Normalization does not use ordered stages
The sequence is correct because 1NF is optional

explanation.ar: المادة بتعرض Normal Forms كمراحل متتابعة: لازم 1NF الأول، وبعدها 2NF، ثم 3NF.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a Star Schema in the course?

options.text: A document collection stored as JSON
A tree of parent-child records
Only normalized sub-dimensions with no fact table
One fact table connected to multiple dimension tables with denormalized dimensions

explanation.ar: Star Schema فيها fact table مركزية متصلة بعدة dimension tables، والـ dimensions فيها denormalized لتبسيط وتسريع الاستعلامات.

questions.question: Why can a Star Schema offer faster query performance according to the comparison in the material?

options.text: It always stores less redundant data
It eliminates dimension tables
It normalizes every dimension into sub-dimensions
Its simpler, flatter structure typically requires fewer joins

explanation.ar: المقارنة بتوضح إن Star Schema أبسط وبتحتاج joins أقل، لذلك query performance عادة أسرع، مقابل redundancy أعلى.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a Snowflake Schema in the course?

options.text: There is no fact table concept
All dimensions are intentionally denormalized
Dimensions are normalized and may be split into sub-dimensions
It stores only semi-structured JSON

explanation.ar: Snowflake Schema بتعمل normalization للـ dimensions، وده ممكن ينتج sub-dimensions ويقلل redundancy.

questions.question: A warehouse design prioritizes storage efficiency and reduced redundancy, and the team accepts more joins and higher structural complexity. Which schema fits the course guidance?

options.text: Star Schema
Hierarchical Model only
Snowflake Schema
Document Model only

explanation.ar: Snowflake أكثر normalized، فـ redundancy أقل وstorage efficiency أعلى، لكن structure أعقد وjoins أكتر.

questions.question: A dashboard workload needs simple query patterns and fast reporting, while some dimension redundancy is acceptable. Which design is favored by the course?

options.text: Star Schema
Weak Entity Model
Snowflake Schema
Unary M:N mapping

explanation.ar: المادة بتذكر Star Schema كأفضل اختيار لـ simple reports/dashboards وبـ faster joins، مع قبول redundancy أعلى.

questions.question: Which comparison is correct according to the Star vs Snowflake table?

options.text: Snowflake always requires fewer joins
Star has more redundancy; Snowflake has less redundancy
Star is more complex to maintain than Snowflake
Star is more normalized than Snowflake

explanation.ar: جدول المقارنة بيذكر Storage: Star = More redundant، Snowflake = Less redundant.

questions.question: Which comparison is correct according to the course?

options.text: Snowflake is intended only for simple dashboards
Star always stores less redundant data
Star is generally easier to maintain; Snowflake is more complex
Snowflake is flatter than Star

explanation.ar: في المقارنة: Maintenance في Star أسهل، بينما Snowflake أكثر تعقيدًا بسبب normalization وتعدد الجداول.

questions.question: In the e-commerce Star Schema lab, which table is specified as the fact table?

options.text: Sales
Products
Customers
Time

explanation.ar: الـ lab بيطلب fact table باسم Sales، مع dimensions مرتبطة زي Customers وProducts وTime.

source.reference: Slide 64 — Implement a Star Schema for an E-commerce Sales Database

questions.question: Which set of dimension tables is explicitly requested in the e-commerce Star Schema lab?

options.text: Customers, Products, and Time
Employee, SalaryAccount, and Medicine
Category, Supplier, and Network
Teacher, Course, and Surgeon

explanation.ar: الـ lab بيحدد dimension tables: Customers, Products, Time حول Sales fact table.

questions.question: For the Product Catalog Snowflake lab, what normalization step is requested?

options.text: Store Category and Supplier as repeating groups
Remove Product information entirely
Merge Category and Supplier into the Sales fact table
Separate Category and Supplier into different tables

explanation.ar: الـ Snowflake lab بيطلب normalize Products table عن طريق فصل Category وSupplier في جداول مختلفة.

source.reference: Slide 64 — Snowflake Schema Product Catalog lab

questions.question: Which constraints are explicitly required in the lab note?

options.text: No constraints because the schema is analytical
Only PRIMARY KEY
Only CHECK and no keys
PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, and CHECK

explanation.ar: الـ lab note بيطلب تطبيق PRIMARY KEY وFOREIGN KEY وUNIQUE، وكمان CHECK constraint على السعر.

source.reference: Slide 64 — Create and Enforce Data Constraints

questions.question: What rule should the CHECK constraint enforce in the Products table according to the lab?

options.text: ProductID must be negative
Price must be greater than zero
Price must always equal zero
Supplier must be stored in the Price column

explanation.ar: المادة بتحدد CHECK constraint للتأكد إن prices في Products أكبر من zero.

questions.question: A Products table accepts a price of -15 even though the lab requirement says prices must be positive. Which missing control best explains the problem?

options.text: A CHECK constraint enforcing Price > 0
A database instance snapshot
A unary relationship
A composite attribute for ProductName

explanation.ar: لو السعر السالب اتقبل، فده معناه إن قاعدة التحقق المطلوبة مش متطبقة؛ الـ CHECK لازم يمنع Price <= 0.

questions.question: What does the retail sales assignment ask students to do after creating a Star Schema?

options.text: Convert it to a Snowflake Schema by normalizing two dimensions
Convert every table to a document model
Remove the fact table
Replace all dimensions with weak entities

explanation.ar: الـ assignment بيطلب أولًا Star Schema، وبعدها تحويله إلى Snowflake عن طريق normalizing 2 dimensions.

questions.question: Why does the assignment ask for sample queries on both Star and Snowflake designs?

options.text: To remove the need for dimensions
To prove both schemas always use the same number of joins
To compare query complexity and performance between the two schema styles
To demonstrate that normalization never affects query structure

explanation.ar: الـ assignment نفسه بيطلب compare query complexity and performance، فكتابة queries على الاتنين بتخلي المقارنة عملية.

questions.question: In the hands-on library lab, which core design activity is required after drawing the ER diagram?

options.text: Remove relationships before creating tables
Store every entity in one multivalued column
Map the ER diagram into relational tables with primary and foreign keys
Convert the system directly to XML only

explanation.ar: الـ library lab بيربط بين ER modeling والتنفيذ العلاقي: بعد رسم ERD لازم يتم mapping لجداول relational مع Primary Keys وForeign Keys.

questions.question: The student-course assignment asks for an ER diagram and relational mapping with what additional requirement?

options.text: Constraints
No keys or relationships
A document database only
A network model instead of tables

explanation.ar: الـ assignment في نهاية الجلسة بيطلب تصميم ERD لنظام student-course registration ثم mapping إلى relational tables مع constraints.
